diagnostic_evidence.quote: The table displays the rate $\alpha$ such that $\overline{I}(p)\sim-|p-p^\star|^\alpha$, estimated based on the data.
with $\overline I$ taking only non-positive values

issues.failure_explanation: The paper's own computation (proof of prop:disk:bifurc, citing Lemma 2.2 of PieKle24) gives, for a real eigenvalue trajectory on the unit disk, I(p) = (a_m pi/2)(1-p^2) J_m(kappa_p)^2, so the simplified indicator of eq:ind_simpl equals \overline I(p) = J_m(kappa_p)^2 >= 0 for real trajectories (any eigenfunction normalization only scales by a positive factor). The prose and captions instead describe the disk's plotted indicator as negative: 'strictly negative for real eigenvalue curves', the fit caption '\overline I(p) ~ -|p-p*|^alpha', and the annulus section's 'with \overline I taking only non-positive values'. Near a cubic bifurcation \overline I(p) ~ +|p-p*|^{2/3} >= 0, so the stated sign is wrong.

failure_location.quote: On the other hand, the indicator is strictly negative for real eigenvalue curves, except at bifurcation points, in agreement with \cref{cor:bifurc}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the sign in the prose and captions to match the formula (state that \overline I = J_m(kappa_p)^2 >= 0 for real disk curves and \overline I ~ +|p-p*|^{2/3} near bifurcations), or relabel the plotted quantity.
issues.overall_effect: Descriptive claims about the sign of the disk indicator \overline I are false as stated; the bifurcation locations (Bessel zeros) and orders (cubic) are unaffected because they depend on the zeros of I, not on its sign.
issues.title: Sign of the disk indicator \overline I misstated as non-positive
issues.why_classification: A single sign correction in descriptive prose/captions; the verified formula and all substantive bifurcation results are preserved, so no mathematical content is lost.

issues.failure_explanation: With the arc-length measure on the boundary circles, \|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_1)}^2 = a_m pi |A_1|^2 and \|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_r)}^2 = a_m pi r |A_r|^2, where A_rho = alpha J_m(kappa rho) + beta Y_m(kappa rho). Hence \|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_1)} = \|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_r)} is equivalent to |A_1| = sqrt(r)|A_r|, not to the bifurcation condition |A_1| = r|A_r| from prop:annulus:bifurc_ord. Under any normalization of the boundary measures the stated equality fails to reproduce the factor r; the correct equivalence is \|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_1)}^2 = r \|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_r)}^2 (i.e., \|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_1)} = sqrt(r) \|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_r)}).

failure_location.quote: By the assumed polar-coordinate separability in \cref{eq:annulus:functions}, this is actually equivalent to $\|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_1)}=\|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_r)}$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Insert the missing factor, stating the equivalence as \|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_1)}^2 = r \|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_r)}^2 (equivalently \|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_1)} = sqrt(r) \|v_p\|_{L^2(\partial B_r)}).
issues.overall_effect: The stated L^2 bifurcation criterion is false as written and would give incorrect bifurcation predictions; the correct L^infinity criterion in prop:annulus:bifurc_ord is unaffected.
issues.title: Annulus L^2 bifurcation criterion missing a factor of sqrt(r)
issues.why_classification: A single missing factor; the correct L^infinity criterion and all bifurcation results survive, so the repair is local and content-preserving.

issues.failure_explanation: For the annulus (n_p = p^2, p > 1), lem:bifurc_ord gives sign(kappa_p') = sign(I(p)) because kappa_p > 0 and \int n_p' |w_p|^2 > 0; combined with eq:ind_simpl, sign(\overline I) = -sign(kappa_p') for p > 1. Hence \overline I becomes positive iff a real trajectory travels to the left (decreasing kappa_p), the opposite of the claimed 'positive iff traveling to the right'. The result that relates the sign of \overline I to the derivative is also lem:bifurc_ord, not cor:bifurc.

failure_location.quote: Therein, we observe that the indicator becomes positive if and only if an eigenvalue trajectory is (i) real and (ii) traveling to the right. Theory confirms this, since \cref{cor:bifurc} relates the sign of $\overline I$ to the sign of the derivative of a real trajectory.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Reverse the claimed relation (for p > 1, \overline I < 0 iff the real trajectory is traveling to the right) and cite lem:bifurc_ord.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed sign-direction relation for the annulus indicator is backwards and 'theory confirms this' is false; the derivative formula itself is unaffected.
issues.title: Annulus indicator sign-direction relation is backwards
issues.why_classification: A sign flip in a descriptive claim; the underlying derivative formula and all bifurcation results are preserved, so the repair is local and content-preserving.
